correctness.rationale: All finite n and fixed weights are covered, including empty and unary cases. Three arches suffice to match any three-bit target, and if fewer arches exist a subsequence constructed from last letters of greedy arches and a missing remainder letter cannot occur. The unique binary arch and unary remainder decomposition gives R(1+A+A²). For both symbol multiplicities >=3, the zero-, one-, and two-arch contributions are 0, 2, and 3(n-2)-2, respectively. The coefficient computation follows from H(u,v)-H(u-1,v-1)=3(u+v)+4. Independent direct exhaustive matching verifies 131071 words and 153 length/composition pairs through length 16; the universal proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly resolves the natural fixed-composition distribution of binary three-subsequence universality for every length, instead of aggregating over all compositions. The unexpected constant absolute number of failures across every interior Hamming-weight class is a robust structural feature with a sharply characterized boundary. It gives an exact conditional probability relevant for constrained words, not just an isolated small computation or rebranding of a standard lemma.
